Pick up the NUC Box and carefully turn it over.

Then grip the top case at all corners.

Lift it off the bottom case.

Step 3: Remove the SATA holder from the bottom case

Unscrew the two black screws.

Turn the bottom case over and remove the other two screws on the opposite side.

Carefully lift the SATA holder off the bottom case.

Place the new SATA holder exactly on the 4 mounting points where the screws go.

Place the bottom case of the NUC Box in the correct position.

Make sure the arrow labeled “front” is actually pointing toward the front.

You can verify this by slightly lifting the front of the NUC Box.

Step 6: Reinsert the screws

Use the screwdriver to screw the screws back into place. Note: do not overtighten the screws. Doing so will make it very difficult to remove them again in the future if needed.

The new bottom case is now installed.

Very Easy

Required Tools:

  • A soft surface – For example, you can use a towel
  • Spudger
  • Micro-screwdriver

Step 1: Remove the Battery Cover

Place the SHIFTphone upside down on a soft surface.

This prevents scratches on the SHIFTphone.

Then, remove the battery cover using the opener at the side of the battery cover.

Step 2: Remove the Battery

Place the SHIFTphone with the camera facing up on a soft surface.

Take the opener and position one end in the middle underneath the battery.

Then make a 45-degree movement with the opener and lift the battery up.

Step 3: Remove the 8 Screws

Carefully unscrew all 8 screws.

Use a suitable screwdriver to prevent damage.

Set the screws aside so you don’t lose them.

Step 4: Remove the Screws at the Bottom of the SHIFTphone

Hold the SHIFTphone firmly on both sides.

Unscrew the fasteners at the bottom.

Apply just enough force to unscrew them.

Step 5: Use the Spudger to Remove the Screen Display from the Case

Use a spudger to carefully detach the screen.

Run it along the edges to unclip the clips.

Do not detach the screen without first loosening everything.

Step 6: Unscrew the 2 Screws, Remove the Metal Bar, and Unclip the Main FPC Cable

Unscrew the 2 screws.

Remove the metal bar after you’ve unscrewed the screws.

Unclip the main FPC cable from the case.

Step 7: Remove the Bottom Daughterboard

Unscrew the fasteners of the board.

Carefully lift the board up.

Gently disconnect the cables.

Step 8: Remove the Long Antenna Cable

Check where the antenna cable is secured and how it is routed within the device.

Gently detach the antenna cable from the connectors.

Carefully pull the cable out of its routing without damaging it.

Step 9: Install the New Long Antenna Cable, Also Secure to the Bottom Daughterboard

Route the new antenna cable in the same path as the old cable.

Firmly connect the cable to the appropriate connectors.

Attach it to the bottom daughterboard and ensure everything is secured properly.

Step 10: Reinstall the Bottom Daughterboard

Place the board back in its position.

Reconnect all cables.

Secure the board tightly with screws.

Step 11: Reinsert the Metal Bar and Reattach Everything

Reinsert the main FPC cable.

Place the metal bar back in the correct position.

Tighten the two screws again.

Step 12: Reinstall the Screen Display onto the Case

Carefully place the screen display back onto the case.

Press the screen firmly along the edges.

Check that the screen is securely attached all around.

Step 13: Reinsert the Battery

Place the battery back into the SHIFTphone.

Install it correctly into the SHIFTphone.

The SHIFT logo should be facing up, with the + and – at the top left.

Step 14: Reattach the Battery Cover

Place the SHIFTphone upside down again on a soft surface.

Take the battery cover and place it back on the SHIFTphone correctly.

Press down at 8 points to ensure the battery cover is securely attached.

45 min
Difficult

  • A soft surface – For example, you can use a towel
  • A small container to store the screws – Make sure you don’t lose the screws
  • Heatsink
  • Screwdriver
  • Spudger (or a similar plastic tool)
  • Thermal paste with a spatula
  • Metal cleaner
  • Wet wipes
  • Microfiber cleaning cloth

Step 1: Remove the screws

Place the NUC Box upside down on a soft surface.

This prevents scratches on the NUC Box.

Then remove all screws using the screwdriver.

Step 2: Remove the bottom cover

Pick up the NUC Box and carefully turn it over.

Then grip the top cover at all corners.

Lift it off from the bottom part.

Step 3: Remove the motherboard

Unscrew the two black screws on both sides.

Disconnect the WiFi antennas from the WiFi module.

Carefully lift the motherboard on both sides and raise it up.

Step 4: Remove the fan from the motherboard

Place the motherboard on a soft surface with the fan facing upward.

Remove the three screws and disconnect the two cables. Note: the two screws on the right side do not fully come out of the component.

Then carefully lift the fan off the motherboard.

Step 5: Remove the heatsink

Carefully remove the screws from the heatsink.

Gently move the heatsink to check if it is loose.

Carefully lift the heatsink on both sides. It may feel slightly stuck due to the sticky thermal paste.

Step 6: Remove the old thermal paste

Remove the old thermal paste from the heatsink.

Use the spatula for this. Afterwards, use wet wipes to remove any remaining thermal paste.

To fully clean the heatsink, use the microfiber cloth with metal cleaner.

Step 7: Apply new thermal paste

Apply a small amount of thermal paste to the spatula.

Spread the thermal paste evenly over the CPU.

Make sure you no longer see any reflective surface on the CPU.

Step 8: Install the new heatsink

Carefully place the new heatsink in position.

Make sure not to shift the heatsink after placing it down.

Tighten the heatsink screws.

Step 9: Reinstall the fan

Place the new fan in the correct position.

Tighten the screws.

Carefully reconnect the cables. They only fit one way.

Step 10: Reinstall the motherboard into the top cover case

Place the motherboard back at a slight angle and gently press it into the correct position. Make sure the WiFi antennas remain above the motherboard.

Reconnect the WiFi antennas to the WiFi module.

Secure the motherboard by tightening the two black screws.

Step 11: Reattach the bottom cover

Place the bottom of the NUC Box back into position.

Make sure the arrow labeled “front” is pointing toward the actual front of the device.

You can verify this by slightly lifting the NUC Box at the front.

Step 12: Reinstall the screws

Use the screwdriver to fasten the screws back into place. Note: do not overtighten the screws. Overtightening may make it difficult to remove them again in the future if needed.

The new bottom cover is now installed.

Well done!
